findings.description: The shared per-netloc Deferred is awaited directly by every request waiting on the same host's robots.txt. maybe_deferred_to_future adds a callback to the Deferred that returns None, so the result chain is consumed after the first waiter. Later waiters get None, and rp_dfd.callback(rp) hands the parser to the first waiter only. Other concurrent requests to that host then see rp=None in process_request_2 and skip the robots.txt check, so forbidden URLs are crawled. The removed per-waiter Deferred forwarded the result to each waiter without consuming the shared chain.
findings.suggestion: Restore a per-waiter Deferred that is fired from a callback on the shared Deferred, and return the result from that callback so the chain value is preserved.
findings.title: Awaiting the shared Deferred directly breaks for multiple concurrent waiters
